title: About
text:
I’m a software architect working on CAM software and AI integration, with a PhD in computer science from FEMTO-ST / Université de Franche-Comté (deep learning and digital holography for precision measurement).
This site is where I think in public: essays from my LinkedIn newsletter AI, Honestly, working papers, and notes on AI on the shop floor.
Opinions here are my own and not those of my employer.

title: Time Is the One Thing AI Doesn’t Compress
text: In this newsletter I have mostly written about how AI changes processes, and how a company should reinvent itself around it. One aspect I never touched: time.

title: Time Is the One Thing AI Doesn’t Compress
section: The feeling of having no time
text:
The feeling of having no time
When we use AI (and I include myself first), we want to do more, always faster, as if we had no time anymore. That feeling is only a feeling, and it may make us lose more than we gain.
Learning takes time. That time is almost incompressible, because learning means understanding.

To solve a problem, spend most of your time understanding it.

title: Time Is the One Thing AI Doesn’t Compress
text:
The first signs
Someone answered one of my questions with “I don’t know, Claude Code did it.” For me, that is one of the first signs that we didn’t take the time to really get into the problem.

title: Fewer Coefficients: Why We Need Less Data, Not More
text:
We keep producing more data, only for it to end up in dashboards. That’s not what we need.
Fit a polynomial of degree n-1 through n points and it hits every one of them, yet swings wildly in between (Runge’s phenomenon). A low-order fit

\hat f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{p} a_k x^k, \qquad p \ll n,

captures the shape and predicts where we haven’t measured.
A useful test: does this output change a decision? If a dashboard tile never alters what anyone does, it’s a coefficient that isn’t pulling its weight.

title: Seeing Is Not Rebuilding
text: In one paragraph. Being intelligent doesn’t let us rebuild a complex system just by looking at it. The limit is missing information, not missing intelligence. A far more powerful AI gets closer to that limit, but it hits the same limit.
